outcome (prognosis, persistent neurological deficits, vessel recanalization)
cohort: The study included 11 patients with Cerebral Venous Thrombosis (CVT), comprising 7 women and 4 men, with an average age of 43.5 years (range 23-69 years).
finding: Hemorrhagic cortical infarctions, influenced by the location and type of brain lesions, were associated with the worst prognosis and the highest rate of persistent neurological deficits.
